message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.55,"fairness_assessment":"A preference-based collective vote is appropriate because the three options represent competing but legitimate community priorities; fairness improves if funding needs, expected usage, and recurring costs are explicitly evaluated rather than relying on an equal split.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Supports Option A: expanding the youth book collection, while facing concerns about whether purchases will match users' needs and be sufficiently used.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Supports Option B: creating an open-access digital space, while needing to account for maintenance, replacement, security, and user-support costs.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Supports Option C: dividing the grant equally between books and digital access, though an equal division may underfund both projects and lacks a needs-based rationale.","influence":0.34}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"Use a ranked-choice or scored social-choice process after jointly assessing demand, accessibility, implementation feasibility, and total long-term costs. The result should permit a tailored allocation or phased pilot rather than imposing an arbitrary 50/50 split, with a review point to adjust funding based on actual usage."}
